title: Versality is stable under generalization
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work with $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal F$ be fibred in groupoids on their big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site]. A category fibred in groupoids assigns a groupoid $\mathcal F(T)$ to each scheme $T$ over the base, with pullback functors and coherent identity and composition isomorphisms. Assume that for every base scheme $T$ and $a,b\in\mathcal F(T)$ the presheaf $T'\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}(a|_{T'},b|_{T'})$ is represented by an algebraic space over $T$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume also that for every diagram of base algebras $A\to B\leftarrow B'$ with $B'\to B$ surjective and square-zero kernel, restriction gives an equivalence $\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_B B'))\simeq\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)}\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B')$, where the right side retains the specified isomorphism over $B$ and arrows compatible with it. Assume limit preservation: for every small directed inverse system of affine base schemes with limit $T$, objects over $T$ descend to a stage, isomorphisms between stage objects descend to a sufficiently late common stage, and equality of such isomorphisms over $T$ holds at a sufficiently late common stage. Let $U$ be of finite type over $S$ and $x\in\mathcal F(U)$. A point $u\in U$ is of finite type if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)\to U$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. For $x\in\mathcal F(U)$, versality at $u$ means: for every surjection $A'\to A$ of Artinian local base algebras with common residue field identified with $\kappa(u)$ and nilpotent kernel, every map $\operatorname{Spec}A\to U$ reducing to $u$, and every $y'\in\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}A')$ with a specified isomorphism $y'|_A\cong x|_A$, there is a lift $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ and an isomorphism $y'\cong x|_{A'}$ inducing the specified one. Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize; local means having a unique maximal ideal, and all maps respect the residue-field identifications. For finite type points $u,u_0\in U$ with $u_0\in\overline{\{u\}}$, if $x$ is versal at $u_0$, then $x$ is versal at $u$.

source.place: Tag 0G2K (lemma-generalization-versality), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; definitions definition-RS-star and definition-versal.

proof.text: Choose an affine member $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ of a finite-type affine cover of $U$ containing $u_0$; its coordinate ring is finitely generated over $\Lambda$ by the definition of finite type. It also contains $u$, since every open containing a specialization contains its generalizations. Versality is unchanged by this restriction: a map from an Artinian local spectrum centered at either point factors through any open neighbourhood of that point, because its spectrum has a single point. Replace $U$ by $U_0$.

source.place: Tag 0G2K (lemma-generalization-versality), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; definitions definition-RS-star and definition-versal.

proof.text: Suppose $x$ is not versal at $u$. The single-point obstruction lemma gives $j:U\hookrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $y\in\mathcal F(T)$ and $\theta:x\cong j^*y$, with $R\to R_0$ surjective and square-zero kernel, for which no neighbourhood of $u$ admits a retraction arrow $y\to x$ inducing $\theta^{-1}$. Its hypotheses hold because $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, $U$ is affine finite type, $u$ is a finite type point, and the assumed fibre-product equivalence is (RS*).

source.place: Tag 0G2K (lemma-generalization-versality), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; definitions definition-RS-star and definition-versal.

proof.text: Order the finitely generated $\Lambda$-subalgebras $R_i\subset R$ by inclusion. Finite unions of generating sets give upper bounds; each element of $R$ belongs to a stage. Thus their union is $R$ and is their ring colimit: compatible ring maps glue uniquely element by element. The affine-limit theorem identifies $T=\varprojlim\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. Limit preservation descends $y$ to $x^\prime$ over some $U^\prime=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, with a specified isomorphism on $T$. Enlarge $R_i$ by lifts of finitely many $\Lambda$-algebra generators of $R_0$, so $R_i\to R_0$ is surjective. Its kernel is a subideal of the square-zero kernel of $R\to R_0$. Hence $j^\prime:U\hookrightarrow U^\prime$ is a first order thickening, $U^\prime$ is finite type over $S$, and the arrows $x\to y\to x^\prime$ lie over $U\to T\to U^\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0G2K (lemma-generalization-versality), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; definitions definition-RS-star and definition-versal.

proof.text: Apply versal base change over $\Lambda$ to $x$ and $x^\prime$. It gives an algebraic space $Z$ representing triples $(a:V\to U,b:V\to U^\prime,\alpha:a^*x\cong b^*x^\prime)$, projections $p,q$, and the section $i:U\to Z$ determined by the specified reduction isomorphism, with $p i=\operatorname{id}$ and $q i=j^\prime$. The cited thickening clause ensures $i(u_0)$ is a finite type point and gives an open $O\subset Z$ containing it on which $q$ is smooth. The open $i^{-1}(O)$ contains $u_0$ and therefore $u$.

source.place: Tag 0G2K (lemma-generalization-versality), specialized to an affine Noetherian base; definitions definition-RS-star and definition-versal.

proof.text: Choose a principal affine neighbourhood $D(f_0)\subset U$ of $u_0$ contained in $i^{-1}(O)$, and lift $f_0$ to $f\in R_i$. Restrict $U,U^\prime,T$ to $D(f_0),D(f),D(f)$, respectively. Square-zero ideals lie in every prime, so these corresponding opens have identical underlying spaces and still contain $u$. Apply affine infinitesimal lifting to the smooth map $O\to U^\prime$ (with its original target), the affine thickening $D(f_0)\hookrightarrow D(f)$ and $i|_{D(f_0)}$. It gives $i^\prime:D(f)\to O$ with $q i^\prime$ the inclusion and $i^\prime j^\prime=i$. Pull back the universal isomorphism along $i^\prime$ and invert it to obtain an arrow $x^\prime|_{D(f)}\to x$ over $p i^\prime$, whose reduction is the inverse of $x\to x^\prime$. Composing with $y|_{D(f)}\to x^\prime|_{D(f)}$ gives a retraction arrow to $x$ on a neighbourhood of $u$ in $T$. Its composite with $x\to y$ is the restriction identity by the specified reduction isomorphisms. This contradicts the obstruction and proves versality at $u$.

Step 2: the single-point node's hypotheses hold exactly, including (RS*) in the same wording. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition gives T = lim Spec R_i, limit preservation descends y, and enlarging R_i gives a square-zero kernel, hence a first-order thickening. Step 4: the new 0CXM node applies to (U,x),(U',x') through its thickening clause, so i(u_0) is a finite-type point with q smooth on O, and i^{-1}(O) contains u. Step 5: 04AM lifting on D(f_0) into D(f) gives i'; inverting the pulled-back universal isomorphism and composing with y->x' gives a retraction that contradicts 0G2J(3). proof_deps equals the union of the uses and there is no cycle. New node 0G2J: true specialization of the source to an affine Noetherian base; the no-retraction clause is equivalent to the source's (3); tested on F = point over k[t]/t^2, where k[t]/t^3 has no splitting. New node 0CXM: assumes (RS*) and limit preservation, which are stronger than (RS) and the diagonal being locally of finite type, so it is true. The section i is locally of finite type because p is, so it preserves finite-type points. Duplicate check: it is the arbitrary-Noetherian-base generalization of the existing Z-only lem-sfb-artin-versal-base-change-smooth, which cannot apply here because a finite-type Lambda-scheme need not be of finite type over Z.
